## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py — GAP-290 enforcement.
4	
5	Rebuilds a fresh DB from the migration history alone and compares core invariants
6	against the committed data/guidebook.db. A divergence means someone wrote directly
7	to the DB and bypassed the migration system, so the committed blob no longer
8	reproduces from its own history.
9	
10	WHY THIS IS A SCRIPT
11	--------------------
12	It used to exist twice — as an inline heredoc in .github/workflows/audit.yml and  [RETIRED-VOCAB-OK]
13	a second, separately-maintained heredoc in scripts/preflight.sh. Two copies of an
14	invariant list is one copy too many: adding a table to one does not add it to the
15	other, and nothing would have told you. This is now the single definition, wired
16	through governance/check-registry.yaml.
17	
18	SCOPE (DR-2026-05-28 / D-4.3-H option 3a, ratified 2026-06-11)
19	--------------------------------------------------------------
20	The gate enforces the CORE INVARIANTS below. They cover all synthesis-bearing
21	content and must reproduce from migration history.
22	
23	The job-owned tables `evidence_source_authors` and `pipeline_runs` are
24	DELIBERATELY EXEMPT: the source-verification scheduled job (resolve-dois.yml /
25	verify-urls.yml) is their authoritative writer and writes them outside the
26	migration framework by design. Do NOT add them to the invariant list.
27	**Adding any new exempt table requires a new DR.**
28	
29	Checks:
30	  C1  the migration history rebuilds without error
31	  C2  PRAGMA user_version matches
32	  C3  each core table's row count matches
33	
34	Usage:
35	    python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py
36	    python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --rebuilt-to /tmp/rebuilt.db
37	    python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --selftest
38	
39	Exit codes: 0 = reproducible, 1 = divergence or rebuild failure, 2 = cannot run.
40	
41	Honours GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH (default data/guidebook.db).
42	"""
43	
44	import argparse
45	import os
46	import shutil
47	import sqlite3
48	import subprocess
49	import sys
50	import tempfile
51	
52	REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
53	
54	# The invariants are DERIVED, not listed. This was six hardcoded table names --
55	# evidence_sources, citation_mining, source_slug_links, gaps, connections, items --
56	# and a handler that turned sqlite3.OperationalError into a silent `skip (no such
57	# table)`. Measured 2026-08-28 against the pending seven-stage rename: ALL SIX
58	# skipped, and the check printed `EXAMINED: 7` while examining one thing, the
59	# schema version. A gate that examined nothing gated nothing (CLAUDE.md §2a), and
60	# the moment it mattered most -- a rename -- it went blind by design.
61	#
62	# The skip existed for a real case ("a table may legitimately not exist in an
63	# older schema version"), but it cannot tell that case from "renamed and nobody
64	# swept me", which is the case this gate is FOR. Under a version mismatch,
65	# schema_version already reports it, so nothing is lost by making absence loud.
66	#
67	# Comparing every table costs nothing measurable (~66 COUNT(*) over a 3.6 MB DB)
68	# and is strictly stronger: measured the same day, a fresh rebuild reproduces the
69	# committed database on every table, so this cries no wolf.
70	SCHEMA_VERSION_INVARIANT = ("PRAGMA user_version", "schema_version")
71	
72	EXEMPT_TABLES = ("evidence_source_authors", "pipeline_runs")
73	
74	# Columns whose divergence is bookkeeping rather than substance. Kept separate so
75	# --deep can say "277 rows differ, all of them only in updated_at" instead of
76	# reporting that as content drift and being ignored for crying wolf.
77	VOLATILE_COLUMNS = frozenset({
78	    "created_at", "updated_at", "last_updated",
79	    "created_by_session", "updated_by_session",
80	})
81	
82	# data_migrations is the ledger *of* the rebuild, so comparing its application
83	# provenance compares the run to itself: applied_at is when this run applied each
84	# migration, and the runner stamps notes='rebuilt by runner'. What must match is
85	# which migrations exist and what their content hashed to. Handled by name rather
86	# than by adding "notes"/"applied_at" to VOLATILE_COLUMNS, which would blind the
87	# comparison to genuine drift in any other table carrying a column so named.
88	LEDGER_TABLE = "data_migrations"
89	LEDGER_COLUMNS = ("migration_id", "content_sha")
90	
91	
92	def db_path():
93	    return os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "data", "guidebook.db"))
94	
95	
96	def migrations_fingerprint():
97	    """SHA over every migration file's bytes — the sole input to a rebuild.
98	
99	    If this is unchanged, a rebuild is byte-for-byte the work already done.
100	    """
101	    import hashlib
102	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
103	    # Must be the SAME directory the rebuild replays. This fingerprinted the
104	    # repository's migrations unconditionally while the rebuild it guards honours
105	    # GUIDEBOOK_MIGRATIONS_DIR (scripts/migrate_db.py:42) — so pointing that
106	    # variable anywhere produced a cache key describing one input set and a
107	    # rebuild performed from another, and the mismatch surfaces as a spurious
108	    # FAIL on a BLOCKING gate. Found by the 2026-08-14 retirement planning pass
109	    # (remediation workplan §6, "a trap found in passing").
110	    migrations = os.environ.get(
111	        "GUIDEBOOK_MIGRATIONS_DIR", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "scripts", "migrations"))
112	    for name in sorted(os.listdir(migrations)):
113	        if not name.endswith(".sql"):
114	            continue
115	        digest.update(name.encode())
116	        with open(os.path.join(migrations, name), "rb") as fh:
117	            digest.update(fh.read())
118	    return digest.hexdigest()[:16]
119	
120	
121	def _usable_cache(path):
122	    """Is this cached rebuild safe to compare a BLOCKING gate against?
123	
124	    Existence and non-zero size are not enough. A truncated or half-written file
125	    would be copied in and become the baseline the reproducibility gate measures
126	    the committed DB against — and a corrupt baseline produces a verdict that
127	    means nothing while looking exactly like one that does. Trusting a cache more
128	    than the thing it stands in for is how the defects this session spent its time
129	    on came about.
130	
131	    So: open it, confirm SQLite agrees it is a database, and confirm it carries
132	    the core tables the comparison needs. Cheap (milliseconds) next to a ~45s
133	    rebuild, and a failed probe simply falls through to building fresh.
134	    """
135	    if not (os.path.exists(path) and os.path.getsize(path) > 0):
136	        return False
137	    try:
138	        con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
139	        try:
140	            if con.execute("PRAGMA quick_check").fetchone()[0] != "ok":
141	                return False
142	            present = {n for (n,) in con.execute(
143	                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")}
144	            needed = {"evidence_sources", "citation_mining", "source_slug_links",
145	                      "gaps", "connections", "items"}
146	            return needed <= present
147	        finally:
148	            con.close()
149	    except sqlite3.Error:
150	        return False
151	
152	
153	def rebuild(target, cache=True):
154	    """C1 — rebuild from migration history alone.
155	
156	    COST. A rebuild is ~33s and dominates the board: this check and its --deep
157	    sibling are 66s of the full run's 110s, and they were doing the SAME rebuild
158	    twice because they are two registry entries sharing one input. The registry
159	    note conceded that and shipped it anyway.
160	
161	    The rebuild's only input is the migration files, so it is cached on their
162	    fingerprint. Both checks run in one CI job (the `data` battery), so the second
163	    invocation reuses the first's artifact and the pair costs one rebuild rather
164	    than two. A change to any migration changes the fingerprint and forces a fresh
165	    build, so the cache cannot mask the thing the check exists to detect.
166	    """
167	    if cache:
168	        cached = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(),
169	                              f"guidebook-repro-{migrations_fingerprint()}.db")
170	        if _usable_cache(cached):
171	            try:
172	                shutil.copyfile(cached, target)
173	                return True, f"reused cached rebuild ({os.path.basename(cached)})"
174	            except OSError:
175	                pass  # fall through to a real rebuild

195	def compare(committed_path, rebuilt_path):
196	    """C2/C3 — compare schema version and EVERY table's row count.
197	
198	    Returns (rows, mismatches). A table present in one database and absent from
199	    the other is a MISMATCH, never a skip: that asymmetry is exactly what a
200	    rename with an unswept caller looks like.
201	    """
202	    committed = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{committed_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
203	    rebuilt = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{rebuilt_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
204	    rows, mismatches = [], []
205	
206	    sql, label = SCHEMA_VERSION_INVARIANT
207	    c = committed.execute(sql).fetchone()[0]
208	    r = rebuilt.execute(sql).fetchone()[0]
209	    rows.append((label, c, r, "OK" if c == r else "MISMATCH"))
210	    if c != r:
211	        mismatches.append((label, c, r))
212	
213	    ct, rt = _tables(committed), _tables(rebuilt)
214	    for name in sorted((ct | rt) - set(EXEMPT_TABLES)):
215	        label = f"{name} count"
216	        if name not in ct or name not in rt:
217	            where = "rebuilt only" if name not in ct else "committed only"
218	            rows.append((label, None, None, f"MISMATCH (present in {where})"))
219	            mismatches.append((label, "absent" if name not in ct else "present",
220	                               "present" if name not in ct else "absent"))
221	            continue
222	        c = committed.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % name).fetchone()[0]
223	        r = rebuilt.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % name).fetchone()[0]
224	        rows.append((label, c, r, "OK" if c == r else "MISMATCH"))
225	        if c != r:
226	            mismatches.append((label, c, r))
227	
228	    committed.close()
229	    rebuilt.close()
230	    return rows, mismatches

233	def q(identifier):
234	    """Quote an identifier. Table names reach PRAGMA and ORDER BY from sqlite_master,
235	    so an unquoted interpolation turns an odd-but-legal name into an OperationalError
236	    — a crash where a verdict belongs, which is the conflation this repo just fixed
237	    in render_audit.js."""
238	    return '"' + str(identifier).replace('"', '""') + '"'

243	        "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'")}

246	def schema_objects(conn):
247	    """Views, triggers and indexes, by name -> DDL.
248	
249	    Rows are not the whole database. `v_best_practice` (migration 027/029) carries
250	    the convergence-laundering exclusion in its WHERE clause, so editing that view
251	    in the committed DB changes what the project treats as a best-practice claim
252	    while leaving every row identical. A row-only comparison calls that PASS.
253	    """
254	    return {(t, n): sql for t, n, sql in conn.execute(
255	        "SELECT type, name, sql FROM sqlite_master "
256	        "WHERE type IN ('view','trigger','index') AND sql IS NOT NULL "
257	        "AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'")}

260	def deep_compare(committed_path, rebuilt_path):
261	    """Every table, every row — not just seven scalars.
262	
263	    WHY THIS EXISTS. The core invariants are `PRAGMA user_version` plus COUNT(*)
264	    on six tables. An UPDATE changes no count, so the entire class of "someone
265	    edited values in the committed DB" is invisible to them, and so is any change
266	    to the 56 tables not on the list. CLAUDE.md rule 4 nonetheless says CI "fails
267	    on any divergence", which was never what the comparator did.
268	
269	    Returns (report_rows, substantive, volatile_only), where each report row is
270	    (table, verdict, detail).
271	    """
272	    committed = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{committed_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
273	    rebuilt = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{rebuilt_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
274	    rows, substantive, volatile_only = [], [], []
275	
276	    tc, tr = user_tables(committed), user_tables(rebuilt)
277	    for missing in sorted(tc - tr):
278	        rows.append((missing, "MISSING-IN-REBUILD", "table absent from migration history"))
279	        substantive.append(missing)
280	    for extra in sorted(tr - tc):
281	        rows.append((extra, "EXTRA-IN-REBUILD", "migration history builds a table the DB lacks"))
282	        substantive.append(extra)
283	
284	    for table in sorted(tc & tr):
285	        if table in EXEMPT_TABLES:
286	            rows.append((table, "EXEMPT", "job-owned per DR-2026-05-28"))
287	            continue
288	        cols = [r[1] for r in committed.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({q(table)})")]
289	        rcols = [r[1] for r in rebuilt.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({q(table)})")]
290	        if cols != rcols:
291	            rows.append((table, "SCHEMA-DIFF", f"columns differ: {set(cols) ^ set(rcols)}"))
292	            substantive.append(table)
293	            continue
294	        if table == LEDGER_TABLE:
295	            cols = [c for c in cols if c in LEDGER_COLUMNS]
296	        select = ", ".join(q(c) for c in cols)
297	        # Sort by the SUBSTANTIVE columns first, then the volatile ones. Sorting by
298	        # every column in declaration order pairs rows by whatever comes first, so
299	        # a table whose volatile column is declared early re-sorts when a timestamp
300	        # changes, zip() pairs row 1 against row 2, and the resulting diff smears
301	        # across unrelated columns — reporting a pure updated_at change as CONTENT.
302	        # Ordering on identity first makes a volatile-only edit leave the pairing
303	        # untouched. Where the substantive columns tie, any pairing is equivalent:
304	        # the rows agree on everything non-volatile, so the verdict is volatile
305	        # either way.
306	        ordered = ([c for c in cols if c not in VOLATILE_COLUMNS]
307	                   + [c for c in cols if c in VOLATILE_COLUMNS])
308	        order = ", ".join(q(c) for c in ordered)
309	        # Explicit column list, not SELECT * — the ledger case narrows `cols`, and
310	        # * would return the excluded columns anyway and compare them.
311	        sql = f'SELECT {select} FROM {q(table)} ORDER BY {order}'
312	        cr = committed.execute(sql).fetchall()
313	        rr = rebuilt.execute(sql).fetchall()
314	        if len(cr) != len(rr):
315	            rows.append((table, "COUNT", f"committed={len(cr)} rebuilt={len(rr)}"))
316	            substantive.append(table)
317	            continue
318	        differing_cols, n_rows = {}, 0
319	        for a, b in zip(cr, rr):
320	            if a == b:
321	                continue
322	            n_rows += 1
323	            for i, name in enumerate(cols):
324	                if a[i] != b[i]:
325	                    differing_cols[name] = differing_cols.get(name, 0) + 1
326	        if not differing_cols:
327	            rows.append((table, "OK", ""))
328	            continue
329	        real = {c: n for c, n in differing_cols.items() if c not in VOLATILE_COLUMNS}
330	        summary = ", ".join(f"{c}({n})" for c, n in
331	                            sorted(differing_cols.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:5])
332	        if real:
333	            rows.append((table, "CONTENT", f"{n_rows} rows; {summary}"))
334	            substantive.append(table)
335	        else:
336	            rows.append((table, "TIMESTAMPS", f"{n_rows} rows; {summary}"))
337	            volatile_only.append(table)
338	
339	    # Views/triggers/indexes: DDL, not rows. See schema_objects().
340	    oc, orb = schema_objects(committed), schema_objects(rebuilt)
341	    for key in sorted(set(oc) - set(orb)):
342	        rows.append((f"{key[0]} {key[1]}", "MISSING-IN-REBUILD", "not built by the migrations"))
343	        substantive.append(f"{key[0]} {key[1]}")
344	    for key in sorted(set(orb) - set(oc)):
345	        rows.append((f"{key[0]} {key[1]}", "EXTRA-IN-REBUILD", "migrations build it; the DB lacks it"))
346	        substantive.append(f"{key[0]} {key[1]}")
347	    for key in sorted(set(oc) & set(orb)):
348	        if " ".join(oc[key].split()) != " ".join(orb[key].split()):
349	            rows.append((f"{key[0]} {key[1]}", "DDL", "definition differs from the migrations'"))
350	            substantive.append(f"{key[0]} {key[1]}")
351	
352	    committed.close()
353	    rebuilt.close()
354	    return rows, substantive, volatile_only

451	def selftest():
452	    """Prove the comparator actually fires. Builds two DBs that differ by one row
453	    and asserts a mismatch is reported — the repo's "a gate nobody has watched
454	    fire is not a gate" norm."""
455	    print("=" * 70)
456	    print("migration_reproducibility --selftest")
457	    print("=" * 70)
458	    failures = []
459	
460	    def check(label, condition, detail=""):
461	        if condition:
462	            print(f"  [PASS] {label}")
463	        else:
464	            print(f"  [FAIL] {label}{': ' + detail if detail else ''}")
465	            failures.append(label)
466	
467	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
468	        a = os.path.join(tmpdir, "a.db")
469	        b = os.path.join(tmpdir, "b.db")
470	        for path, extra in ((a, 0), (b, 1)):
471	            con = sqlite3.connect(path)
472	            con.execute("PRAGMA user_version = 42")
473	            for table in ("evidence_sources", "citation_mining", "source_slug_links",
474	                          "gaps", "connections", "items"):
475	                con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {table} (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)")
476	                con.execute(f"INSERT INTO {table} (id) VALUES (1)")
477	            for i in range(extra):
478	                con.execute("INSERT INTO items (id) VALUES (?)", (100 + i,))
479	            con.commit()
480	            con.close()
481	
482	        _, same = compare(a, a)
483	        check("identical DBs report no mismatch", not same, str(same))
484	
485	        _, differ = compare(a, b)
486	        check("a one-row divergence in `items` IS reported",
487	              any(label == "items count" for label, _, _ in differ), str(differ))
488	
489	        # A missing table must be skipped, not crash the comparator.
490	        c = os.path.join(tmpdir, "c.db")
491	        con = sqlite3.connect(c)
492	        con.execute("PRAGMA user_version = 42")
493	        con.commit()
494	        con.close()
495	        rows, _ = compare(c, c)
496	        check("missing tables are skipped, not fatal",
497	              any(r[3].startswith("skip") for r in rows))
498	
499	        # --- deep comparison -------------------------------------------------
500	        # The point of --deep is the case the core invariants are blind to: an
501	        # UPDATE, which changes values while leaving every COUNT identical. These
502	        # two assertions are a matched pair — the second is only meaningful
503	        # because the first shows the core comparator says PASS on the same DBs.
504	        d = os.path.join(tmpdir, "d.db")

515	            con.commit()
516	            con.close()

518	        _, core_mismatches = compare(d, e)
519	        check("core invariants are BLIND to a value-only edit (the gap --deep closes)",
520	              not core_mismatches, str(core_mismatches))
521	
522	        _, substantive, _ = deep_compare(d, e)
523	        check("--deep reports the value-only edit the counts missed",
524	              "t" in substantive, str(substantive))
525	
526	        # A timestamp-only difference must be separated from real content, or the
527	        # check cries wolf on every rebuild and stops being read.

590	        for table in ("evidence_sources", "citation_mining", "source_slug_links",

600	        except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:

603	    print("=" * 70)

2	"""DOI resolution and source verification against evidence_sources v2 schema.
3	
4	Per verification-pipeline-proposal-2026-05-12-v2.md V1.
5	
6	Pipeline phases (run in order, each writes to evidence_sources via write_verification):
7	
8	  Phase 0  PMC extractor — scan pub_title for embedded PMC IDs, write to pmcid column
9	           (no network; pure regex pass)
10	  Phase 1a PMID -> DOI via NCBI ID Converter
11	  Phase 1b PMCID -> DOI via NCBI ID Converter (covers rows populated in Phase 0)
12	  Phase 2a CrossRef structured query (person-authored academic)
13	  Phase 2b CrossRef bibliographic query (corporate-authored academic)
14	  Phase 3  CrossRef type:standard filter (ISO/EN/BSI standards)
15	
16	Acceptance for Phase 2a/2b (academic):
17	  - Author surname (or corporate token) in CrossRef result's first 3 authors / publisher
18	  - Title-word Jaccard overlap >= 0.55 after stopword removal (or 100% for short titles)
19	  - Year matches within +/- 1
20	  - Only one plausible candidate (ambiguity = reject)
21	
22	Acceptance for Phase 3 (standards):
23	  - Publisher contains 'BSI', 'British Standards', 'ISO', or 'CEN'
24	  - Title contains keywords from the source's standard number AND pub_title
25	
26	Skip behavior (applies to all phases):
27	  - doi_resolution_outcome = 'REVERTED'  -> permanently skipped
28	  - doi_resolution_outcome = 'NO-MATCH' within SKIP_NO_MATCH_DAYS -> skipped
29	  - Already has doi -> skipped
30	
31	Writes (all phases use central write_verification function):
32	  - verification_status (VERIFIED / NO-MATCH; not set on transient)
33	  - verified_by_tool (per-phase identifier)
34	  - last_verified_at (ISO timestamp)
35	  - verification_attempt_count (increments)
36	  - doi (only when found, never clobbers existing)
37	  - pmcid (only when found, never clobbers existing)
38	  - verification_note (only when supplied)
39	  - doi_resolution_outcome (RESOLVED / NO-MATCH)
40	  - updated_at, updated_by_session
41	
42	Env vars:
43	  GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH   path to SQLite (default: data/guidebook.db)
44	  MAX_RESOLVE         max candidates per CrossRef phase (default: 500)
45	  SKIP_NO_MATCH_DAYS  days before retrying a NO-MATCH (default: 30)
46	  RATE_LIMIT          seconds between API calls (default: 5.0 — conservative)
47	"""

105	    """Atomic verification-state write.
106

108	    pmcid with NULL. Always increments verification_attempt_count. Always sets
109	    verified_by_tool, last_verified_at, updated_at, updated_by_session.
110	
111	    D-0157: when this function sets a status it must also set the standing
112	    columns, or it writes a row that violates the invariants the same decision
113	    installed. A VERIFIED row with no disposition fails I1; a tool-established
114	    row with no method loses the fact that a tool established it. Both are set
115	    here rather than at the call sites, so a future phase cannot forget.
116	    """
117	    ts = ts or time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.gmtime())
118	
119	    sets = ["verified_by_tool = ?", "last_verified_at = ?",

557	            conn.execute("DELETE FROM evidence_source_authors WHERE ref_id=?", (ref_id,))

611	def crossref_doi_lookup(doi):
612	    """Fetch full CrossRef metadata by DOI. Returns item or None on transient error."""
613	    if not doi:
614	        return None
615	    url = f"https://api.crossref.org/works/{urllib.parse.quote(doi, safe='/')}"
616	    try:
617	        data = fetch_json(url, timeout=15)
618	        return data.get("message")
619	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
620	        if e.code == 404:
621	            return None  # DOI not in CrossRef (rare but possible)
622	        # 403/429/5xx: transient — caller will retry next run
623	        return None
624	    except Exception:
625	        return None

630	def phase_0_pmc_extractor(conn, ts):
631	    """Extract PMC IDs from pub_title field into the pmcid column.
632	
633	    Pure regex pass — no network calls. Writes pmcid via write_verification with
634	    no verification_status (since extraction alone isn't verification).
635	    """
636	    rows = conn.execute(f"""
637	        SELECT ref_id, pub_title, pmcid FROM {TABLE}
638	        WHERE (pmcid IS NULL OR pmcid = '')
639	        AND pub_title LIKE '%PMC%'
640	    """).fetchall()
641	
642	    extracted = 0
643	    for r in rows:
644	        m = re.search(r"PMC(\d+)", r["pub_title"] or "")
645	        if not m:
646	            continue
647	        pmcid = f"PMC{m.group(1)}"
648	        # Direct UPDATE — extraction is not a verification event, just a backfill.
649	        conn.execute(
650	            f"UPDATE {TABLE} SET pmcid=?, updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE ref_id=?",
651	            (pmcid, ts, SESSION, r["ref_id"])
652	        )
653	        print(f"  PMC extract: {r['ref_id']} <- {pmcid}")
654	        extracted += 1
655	
656	    conn.commit()
657	    return extracted

665	        return 1

668	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
669	    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	scripts/research/retrieval_log.py — persist what was actually retrieved.
4	
5	WHY
6	---
7	On 2026-08-19 the first research batch after the restart wrote FABRICATED author
8	lists onto all five of its admissions, and stamped them
9	`verification_status='VERIFIED'`, `verified_by_tool='crossref'`,
10	`verification_method='tool'`, `metadata_quality='COMPLETE'`.
11	
12	The retrieval had genuinely happened — the reference counts stored alongside match
13	Crossref exactly, and those numbers exist nowhere but that payload. The author
14	array was in the same JSON object and was overwritten from memory.
15	
16	Nothing could detect it, for one structural reason:
17	
18	    verification_method='tool' was a SELF-ASSERTION WITH NO ARTEFACT BEHIND IT.
19	
20	No gate could tell an executed retrieval from a claimed one, because the evidence
21	of the retrieval was never kept. Finding it took an adversarial pass and five
22	agents. With the payload on disk it is a one-line diff.
23	
24	Owner ruling, 2026-08-19: "the repository has more than enough room to store
25	scratchpad logs if they're ever needed. it is very unlikely we will ever have to
26	look through them unless we are auditing for fidelity."
27	
28	That is exactly the value profile of this log — near-zero read frequency, and
29	irreplaceable in the one case that matters.
30	
31	USE
32	---
33	    from retrieval_log import fetch
34	    payload = fetch("https://api.crossref.org/works/10.xxxx/yyy", session=S,
35	                    purpose="crossref metadata for REF-00965")
36	
37	`fetch` returns the parsed JSON *and* writes the raw bytes under
38	`retrieval-log/<session>/`, with a manifest line recording url, sha256, byte
39	count, HTTP status, and the UTC timestamp. Writes happen BEFORE the caller sees
40	the data, so a caller cannot log a different payload than the one it acted on.
41	`fetch` returns None -- but STILL writes the artefact and manifest line -- for a
42	non-2xx status as well as for a transport failure or an unparseable body: a 404
43	or a publisher interstitial is retrieved evidence of a failed retrieval, not
44	absence of evidence, and CLAUDE.md 5(c) is the reason that distinction is kept
45	rather than dropped along with the rest of the failure.
46	
47	    python3 scripts/research/retrieval_log.py --verify-authors --session <id>
48	
49	verifies stored authors against the LOGGED payload — offline, no network, and
50	authoritative as-of-retrieval rather than as-of-audit. That distinction matters:
51	re-fetching at audit time cannot detect a record that was correct when written and
52	has since been corrected upstream, nor can it run when the API is unreachable.
53	"""

1123	def _index_by_doi(payloads):
1124	    """Every logged payload that identifies a DOI, whatever service produced it.
1125	
1126	    Until 2026-09-02 this read `message.DOI` alone — the shape Crossref returns for
1127	    a single work. Unpaywall files the DOI at top level and its authors under
1128	    `z_authors`; a Crossref SEARCH files works under `message.items`. Three of this
1129	    batch's eight sources were logged only in those shapes, and the verifier
1130	    reported them as "NO LOGGED RETRIEVAL … not verifiable offline" — a shrug
1131	    printed over evidence that was sitting on disk. An indexer that sees one
1132	    vendor's envelope and calls the rest unlogged is CLAUDE.md 2(a) at the input.
1133	
1134	    Richer envelopes win: a Crossref work carries volume/issue/page that Unpaywall
1135	    does not, so it must not be displaced by a thinner record of the same DOI.
1136	    """
1137	    ranked = {}
1138	    def offer(doi, msg, rank):
1139	        if not doi:
1140	            return
1141	        doi = str(doi).strip().lower()
1142	        if doi and rank >= ranked.get(doi, (-1, None))[0]:
1143	            ranked[doi] = (rank, msg)
1144	
1145	    for _url, m in payloads.items():
1146	        if not isinstance(m, dict):
1147	            continue
1148	        msg = m.get("message")
1149	        if isinstance(msg, dict) and msg.get("DOI"):
1150	            offer(msg["DOI"], msg, 3)                       # Crossref, single work

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/emit_data_migration.py — create a properly-named data-migration file.

Per GAP-290 resolution. The migration system (scripts/migrate_db.py) requires
data migrations to be named:

    scripts/migrations/data_{YYYYMMDDHHMMSS}_{session-slug}.sql

This script generates one for you. Two concurrent sessions will produce files
with different timestamps and can both land cleanly on `main`.

Usage:

    # Pipe SQL from stdin
    cat my_changes.sql | python3 scripts/emit_data_migration.py \\
        --session session_2026-05-11g-citation-mining.md \\
        --summary "add 14 evidence_sources from REF-00710 backward mining"

    # Read from a file
    python3 scripts/emit_data_migration.py \\
        --session session_2026-05-11g-citation-mining.md \\
        --summary "cleanup orphan source_slug_links rows" \\
        --input cleanup.sql

    # Output path printed to stdout; the file is committed by you afterward.

The SQL body is wrapped in a single transaction (BEGIN ... COMMIT) so partial
failure rolls back. A frontmatter header with metadata is prepended.

Validation:
  - Refuses if the resulting filename would already exist (timestamp collision —
    rare, sleep 1s and retry)
  - Refuses if the SQL is empty
  - Warns if the SQL contains DROP / TRUNCATE / DELETE without WHERE
"""

import os
import re
import sys
import time

    (re.compile(r"\bTRUNCATE\b", re.I), "TRUNCATE"),
    (re.compile(r"\bDELETE\s+FROM\s+\w+\s*;", re.I), "DELETE without WHERE clause"),
    (re.compile(r"\bUPDATE\s+\w+\s+SET\s+[^;]+;", re.I), "UPDATE — check WHERE clause"),

# It was also INERT ON THE SANCTIONED WRITE PATH. Its Form-1 regex matched `col = 'X'`

    tracks single-quoted-string state, including the doubled `''` escape, and

    cannot correctly split a field containing `datetime('now')` — that case
    is in this module's own false-negative test list (see selftest), so
    csv is not a drop-in replacement here. Kept as-is.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py — capture a research batch out of a scratch DB.

DR-2026-08-19 §12.0 (F3). The research write path is a session-scoped scratch
copy of the database: `db.py` writes to it under GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, so every
write-time refusal stays live (R9 duplicate-DOI lookups, H05/H07, CHECK
constraints, real exec_id allocation) instead of being reimplemented against a
renderer. This tool then extracts the delta as SQL, which feeds the ordinary
`emit_data_migration.py --input` and its ENUM/RANGE guards.

    python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py --scratch batch01.db --out batch01.sql

Both databases are opened read-only. This tool never writes to either one; the
only canonical write in a research session remains `migrate_db.py`.

The walk is additive by design. A row present in canonical but absent from the
scratch is REFUSED rather than rendered as a DELETE: a research batch adds
evidence, and a missing row means the scratch drifted from the canonical base
(usually a stale copy), which is a mistake to surface, not to replay.

ONE NARROW EXCEPTION, opt-in (2026-09-26). Some db.py writers delete on purpose --
`unlink-admission` removes a wrong search_admissions edge -- and an additive-only
capture made that sanctioned write impossible to ship. `--allow-delete TABLE` renders
the missing rows of TABLE as DELETEs, and only when a writer in scripts/ actually
deletes from TABLE (dbcore.deletable_tables, derived from the writers the way the
capture set is). Every other missing row is still refused, so a stale copy is still

252	def discover_data_migrations() -> list:
253	    """Return ordered list of (timestamp, migration_id, path) for data migrations.
254	
255	    Baseline convention (per DR-2026-05-15): when a baseline schema migration
256	    is present, data migrations with timestamps preceding the baseline are
257	    skipped — the baseline already contains the data they would have loaded.
258	    The cutoff is encoded as `BASELINE_DATA_CUTOFF_TS`, refreshed whenever a
259	    new baseline is committed.
260	    """
261	    # 2026-08-12: 057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql bakes in the FULL schema and data, and
262	    # every earlier migration is frozen at _archived/scripts/migrations/. The cutoff
263	    # sits past the last archived data migration (20260812083254) so nothing
264	    # pre-baseline is looked for. It stays as a guard rather than being deleted: if a
265	    # pre-baseline file is ever restored to this directory by mistake, it is skipped
266	    # instead of replayed on top of a database that already contains its effect.
267	    BASELINE_DATA_CUTOFF_TS = "20260812083255"
268	    out = []
269	    bv = baseline_version()
270	    for path in sorted(MIGRATIONS_DIR.glob("data_*.sql")):
271	        m = DATA_PATTERN.match(path.name)
272	        if m:
273	            ts = m.group(1)
274	            if bv is not None and ts < BASELINE_DATA_CUTOFF_TS:
275	                continue  # pre-baseline; data is in baseline already
276	            migration_id = path.stem
277	            out.append((ts, migration_id, path))
278	    out.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
279	    return out

285	def build_plan() -> list:
286	    """The faithful replay order, as a flat list of steps.
287	
288	    Returns [("schema", version, path), ("data", ts, migration_id, path), ...].
289	
290	    THE DEFAULT is what it has always been: every schema migration, then every
291	    data migration. That is right almost always, because schema precedes the
292	    data it shapes.
293	
294	    IT IS WRONG WHENEVER A SCHEMA MIGRATION RENAMES OR DROPS SOMETHING THAT
295	    COMMITTED DATA MIGRATIONS STILL NAME. Data migrations are immutable, so they
296	    keep writing to the old name forever; a schema-phase rename runs first and
297	    they die on replay. Migration 025 hit this from the other side and had to
298	    withdraw a data migration to escape it. The 055 rename hit it from this side
299	    across 19 data migrations spanning two months, where withdrawal is not
300	    available.
301	
302	    A numbered schema migration may therefore declare, on its own line:
303	
304	        -- AFTER_DATA: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS
305	
306	    meaning: this migration, and every migration numbered after it, applies only
307	    once the data migrations up to that timestamp have replayed. That is not a
308	    special case bolted on for one rename — it is the real chronology, which the
309	    numbered/timestamped split cannot otherwise express. Several markers may be
310	    present; each opens another data segment.
311	    """
312	    schema_migs = discover_schema_migrations()
313	    data_migs = discover_data_migrations()
314	    marks = []
315	    for i, (_v, path) in enumerate(schema_migs):
316	        m = AFTER_DATA_PATTERN.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
317	        if m:
318	            marks.append((i, m.group(1)))
319	
320	    plan, si, di = [], 0, 0
321	    for idx, cutoff in marks:
322	        plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:idx]]
323	        si = idx
324	        while di < len(data_migs) and data_migs[di][0] <= cutoff:
325	            plan.append(("data",) + data_migs[di])
326	            di += 1
327	    plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:]]
328	    plan += [("data",) + d for d in data_migs[di:]]
329	    return plan

        for stmt in [s for s in code3.split(";\n") if s.strip()]:
            con.execute(stmt)
        got3 = con.execute("SELECT * FROM evidence_sources ORDER BY ref_id").fetchall()
        con.close()
        con = sqlite3.connect(scratch)
        want3 = con.execute("SELECT * FROM evidence_sources ORDER BY ref_id").fetchall()
        con.close()
        check("replay with the deletion reproduces the scratch exactly", got3 == want3,
              f"{got3} vs {want3}")
        dbcore.deletable_tables = lambda _conn: set()
        rc = 0
        try:
            emit(scratch, canon, os.path.join(tmp, "y.sql"), allow_delete=["evidence_sources"])
        except SystemExit as e:
            rc = 1
            check("--allow-delete on a table no writer deletes from is refused",
                  "no sanctioned writer" in str(e), str(e))
        check("--allow-delete without a deleting writer refused", rc == 1)
        dbcore.deletable_tables = _real_deletable

    dbcore.writable_tables = _real_writable
    print("\n--- emit_batch_sql selftest ---")
    for name, ok, detail in results:
        print("  %s: %s%s" % ("PASS" if ok else "**FAIL**", name,
                              ("  [%s]" % detail) if not ok else ""))
    print("\nRESULTS: %d/%d selftest cases pass" % (len(results) - failures, len(results)))
    print("SELFTEST: %s" % ("FAIL" if failures else "PASS"))
    return 1 if failures else 0


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    p.add_argument("--scratch", help="Session scratch DB written by db.py under GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH")
    p.add_argument("--canonical", default=DEFAULT_CANONICAL,
                   help="Canonical DB to diff against (default: $GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH "
                        "or data/guidebook.db)")
    p.add_argument("--out", default="-", help="Write SQL here ('-' for stdout)")
    p.add_argument("--allow-delete", action="append", default=[], metavar="TABLE",
                   help="Render rows missing from the scratch in TABLE as DELETEs. Only for a "
                        "table a sanctioned writer deletes from (e.g. search_admissions, "
                        "unlink-admission); repeatable. Everything else stays additive.")
    p.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true", help="Run the round-trip tests and exit")
    args = p.parse_args()
    if args.selftest:
        sys.exit(selftest())
    if not args.scratch:

name: Source verification pipeline (V1.2)

# 6-phase pipeline per references/audits/verification-pipeline-proposal-2026-05-12-v2.md:
#   Phase 0  PMC extractor (no network)
#   Phase 1a PMID -> DOI via NCBI
#   Phase 1b PMCID -> DOI via NCBI
#   Phase 2a CrossRef structured (person-author academic)
#   Phase 2b CrossRef bibliographic (corporate-author academic)
#   Phase 3  CrossRef type:standard (ISO/EN/BSI/IEC/PAS standards)
#   Phase 4  CrossRef DOI-lookup metadata enrichment (V1.2 — fills pages,
#            pub_month, language, subtype, citation_count, ORCID, full author
#            lists; promotes metadata_quality AUTHOR-TITLE-ONLY → COMPLETE)
#
# State before/after and per-phase counts are written to the pipeline_runs table
# in data/guidebook.db — consistent with the project's SQLite-first tracking pattern.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      max_resolve:
        description: 'Max candidates per CrossRef phase (2a/2b/3)'
        required: false
        default: '500'
      skip_no_match_days:
        description: 'Days to skip NO-MATCH rows before retrying'
        required: false
        default: '30'
      rate_limit:
        description: 'Seconds between API calls'
        required: false
        default: '5.0'
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'  # Mondays 06:00 UTC

# Prevent overlapping runs racing on data/guidebook.db.
concurrency:
  group: source-verification
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  resolve:
    name: Resolve DOIs and verify sources
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Run verification pipeline
        env:
          GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH: data/guidebook.db
          MAX_RESOLVE: ${{ github.event.inputs.max_resolve || '500' }}

              echo "Push attempt $i failed (transient); backing off..."

content.content:
# The pool query above has no LIMIT; the candidates query below does
    # (LIMIT MAX_VERIFY). The guard must fire on the EFFECTIVE candidate set
    # actually about to be attempted, not the raw pool: MAX_VERIFY=0 (or every
    # candidate resolving transient) left pool_size > 0 while zero verification
    # work would ever be attempted, and the pool_size==0 guard let a
    # `url_verification_runs` row get written for that zero-work run anyway —
    # exactly the outcome the guard exists to prevent. So compute the
    # LIMIT-bounded candidate set FIRST and guard on it.
    candidates = conn.execute(f"""
        SELECT ref_id, url, pub_title
        FROM {TABLE}
        WHERE url IS NOT NULL AND url != ''
        AND verification_status IS NULL
        AND (
          url_resolution_outcome IS NULL
          OR (url_resolution_outcome = 'NO-MATCH' AND last_verified_at < ?)
        )
        ORDER BY ref_id
        LIMIT ?
    """, (cutoff_iso, MAX_VERIFY)).fetchall()

    # Empty candidate set: return before the INSERT below. `url_verification_runs`
    # is not in migration_reproducibility's EXEMPT_TABLES (only
    # evidence_source_authors and pipeline_runs, per DR-2026-05-28), so a run
    # record for zero attempted candidates would still break the
    outcome -> url_resolution_outcome ('MATCHED', 'PARTIAL', 'NO-MATCH', 'DEAD',
                                       'NO-MATCH-WAYBACK', 'WAYBACK-MATCH')
    similarity -> url_match_similarity (float 0..1)
    """
    ts = ts or time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.gmtime())
    sets = ["verified_by_tool = ?",
            "last_verified_at = ?",
            "verification_attempt_count = COALESCE(verification_attempt_count,0) + 1",
            "url_last_fetched = ?",
            "updated_at = ?",
            "updated_by_session = ?"]
    params = ["url-fetch-v1", ts, ts, ts, SESSION]

    if status is not None:
        sets.insert(0, "verification_status = ?")
        params.insert(0, status)
        # D-0157: a status written here must carry its standing columns, or the
        # row violates I1 (VERIFIED+OPEN) the moment it is written. Established
        # by this tool; CLOSED when it succeeded, OPEN when it did not.
        sets.append("verification_disposition = ?")
        params.append("CLOSED" if status == "VERIFIED" else "OPEN")
        sets.append("verification_method = ?")
        params.append("tool")
    if outcome is not None:
        sets.append("url_resolution_outcome = ?")
        params.append(outcome)
    if similarity is not None:
        sets.append("url_match_similarity = ?")
        params.append(float(similarity))
    if note is not None:
        sets.append("verification_note = ?")
        params.append(note)

    params.append(ref_id)
    conn.execute(
        f"UPDATE {TABLE} SET {', '.join(sets)} WHERE ref_id = ?",
        params,
    )

"""Prepare a scratch DB holding the CHAIN's values for every row the bot diverged.

usage: prep_scratch.py <canonical.db> <rebuilt.db> <scratch_out.db> <session_stem>

Nothing here is typed by hand. The divergent set is DERIVED by diffing the canonical
blob against a --rebuild (the chain), and every restored value is read from the
rebuild:

  evidence_sources        for each ref_id whose non-volatile columns differ, copy the
                          rebuild's value of each differing column; stamp updated_at /
                          updated_by_session the way every sanctioned writer does
                          (dbcore.audit) -- the row WAS updated, by this act.
  evidence_source_authors for each ref_id whose author rows differ in any column, delete
                          the canonical rows and insert the rebuild's rows verbatim
                          (id, created_at, created_by_session included): they are the
                          chain's rows, restored, not new rows.

Prints a JSON summary of what it changed.
"""
import json
import shutil
import sqlite3
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import dbcore  # noqa: E402

canon, rebuilt, out, session = sys.argv[1:5]
VOLATILE = {"created_at", "updated_at", "last_updated", "created_by_session", "updated_by_session"}

shutil.copyfile(canon, out)
ca = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{canon}?mode=ro", uri=True)
rb = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{rebuilt}?mode=ro", uri=True)
sc = sqlite3.connect(out)
sc.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")


def cols(con, t):
    return [r[1] for r in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")')]


summary = {"evidence_sources": {}, "evidence_source_authors": {}}

# --- evidence_sources -----------------------------------------------------------
es_cols = cols(ca, "evidence_sources")
assert es_cols == cols(rb, "evidence_sources")
sel = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in es_cols)
c_rows = {r[0]: dict(zip(es_cols, r)) for r in ca.execute(f"SELECT {sel} FROM evidence_sources")}
r_rows = {r[0]: dict(zip(es_cols, r)) for r in rb.execute(f"SELECT {sel} FROM evidence_sources")}
assert set(c_rows) == set(r_rows), "row sets differ: not a value-only divergence"
stamp = dbcore.upd(session)
for ref in sorted(c_rows):
    diff = [c for c in es_cols if c not in VOLATILE and c_rows[ref][c] != r_rows[ref][c]]
    if not diff:
        continue
    sets = {c: r_rows[ref][c] for c in diff}
    sets.update(stamp)
    sc.execute("UPDATE evidence_sources SET " + ", ".join(f'"{c}" = ?' for c in sets)
               + " WHERE ref_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [ref])
    summary["evidence_sources"][ref] = {c: [c_rows[ref][c], r_rows[ref][c]] for c in diff}

# --- evidence_source_authors ----------------------------------------------------
a_cols = cols(ca, "evidence_source_authors")
assert a_cols == cols(rb, "evidence_source_authors")
asel = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in a_cols)


def by_ref(con):
    out = {}
    for r in con.execute(f"SELECT {asel} FROM evidence_source_authors ORDER BY ref_id, position"):
        out.setdefault(r[1], []).append(r)
    return out


ca_a, rb_a = by_ref(ca), by_ref(rb)
for ref in sorted(set(ca_a) | set(rb_a)):
    if ca_a.get(ref) == rb_a.get(ref):
        continue
    sc.execute("DELETE FROM evidence_source_authors WHERE ref_id = ?", [ref])
    for r in rb_a.get(ref, []):
        sc.execute(f"INSERT INTO evidence_source_authors ({asel}) VALUES "
                   f"({', '.join('?' * len(a_cols))})", list(r))
    summary["evidence_source_authors"][ref] = {
        "bot_ids_removed": [r[0] for r in ca_a.get(ref, [])],
        "chain_ids_restored": [r[0] for r in rb_a.get(ref, [])],
    }

sc.commit()
print(json.dumps(summary, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))

content.content:
6. **`migration_reproducibility.EXEMPT_TABLES` holds two names, not one.** `pipeline_runs` (the one
   CLAUDE.md §2 rule 3 names) **and `evidence_source_authors`** — the table the 2026-08-19
   fabrication happened in. A count divergence there is invisible to the blocking gate.

**Cost baseline for comparison.** `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --all` = **41.5 s**, 67 checks,
49 green, 10 NOTHING-IN-SCOPE (6 of them blocking), 8 advisory failures.
`run_checks.py --selftest` = **0.84 s**. Every meta-script below is budgeted under 3 s.

----
                                                    for any row in the corpus
 L3.2  audit stamps present                 OK     created_by_session 9/9
 L3.3  reproducible from migrations         N/A    EXEMPT — evidence_source_authors
                                                    and pipeline_runs are in
                                                    migration_reproducibility.EXEMPT_TABLES
 L3.4  no orphan FK                         OK     PRAGMA foreign_key_check: 0 rows
 L3.5  stage tenancy of each column         N/A    no stage map — see §8
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 VERDICT  1 BROKEN EDGE — L3.1 scope. Repaired writer, unrepaired corpus:
----
- **N5 — off-path writers.** `audit_consolidator.py:248` opens a canonical-defaulting
  path read-write and UPDATEs `item_audit_runs` (:270) with no refusal and no FK pragma.
  `resolve_dois.py:597` UPDATEs `evidence_sources`, outside the only exemption register
  (`migration_reproducibility.py:72`).
- **N6 — the ruled naming route has no instructional caller.** 17 `db.py` verbs are named
  by no skill, no CLAUDE.md, no governance file — including `add-term`, `add-parameter`
----
each other.

**F10 — The gate that enforces "never write the DB directly" compares seven
scalars.** `migration_reproducibility.py` compares `PRAGMA user_version` plus
`COUNT(*)` on six tables, while CLAUDE.md §0 rule 4 says CI "fails on any
divergence". An `UPDATE` changes no count, so value-level edits are invisible, as is
everything in the other 55 tables — demonstrated by tampering with a scratch copy
(a row's `tier` and title rewritten, and a forged `stated` row inserted into
`specifications`) and watching it return `VERDICT: PASS`. `EXEMPT_TABLES` was
decorative: the comparator never enumerated tables, so it was printed and never
applied.

Added `--deep`, wired **advisory** as `migration_reproducibility_deep`. It compares
every table and every row, and separates timestamp-only divergence from content so
it does not cry wolf. What it finds looks like an **incomplete exemption list
rather than a hand-edited DB**:
----

**3. Never write `data/guidebook.db` directly.** Migrations only:
`scripts/emit_data_migration.py` → `scripts/migrate_db.py`. Append-only and immutable once
committed — fix forward with a compensating migration.
→ Enforced by `migration_reproducibility` (blocking), **which compares row COUNTS only** — an UPDATE
is invisible to it. `migration_reproducibility_deep` compares every row and is **advisory**.
→ **And the repository breaks this rule on a timer.** The scheduled `source-verification` workflow
(`.github/workflows/resolve-dois.yml`) commits a `pipeline_runs` row straight into the blob, and it
also UPDATEs `evidence_sources` and rewrites `evidence_source_authors` when a phase fires (bot commit
`c4c8463` flipped a source's `author_count_is_complete` with no migration and no saved payload).
`migration_reproducibility` sees neither: both author and run tables sit in its `EXEMPT_TABLES`, and
an UPDATE never changes a row count. A rebuild does not reproduce it, and **every open PR
touching the DB inherits a binary conflict when it fires** (2026-09-07 did exactly that to PR #128).
Resolving such a conflict costs nothing: take the branch's DB and let the next run re-emit.

---

**Scope caveat, added 2026-08-05.** Step 2 above originally read "compare row counts",
which reads as a full comparison and is not one. It compares counts on six tables, so
an `UPDATE` changes nothing it can see, and neither does anything in the other 55
tables. The migrations-only rule (CLAUDE.md §0 rule 4) is absolute; this gate is its
detection floor, not its full extent. The complete comparison exists as
`migration_reproducibility_deep`, advisory pending an owner decision.

What this catches: a session that wrote to the DB directly (e.g., via `db.py add-source`) without also emitting a corresponding migration. The migration history would then no longer reproduce the committed DB. The check blocks the push and surfaces the diff.

# E-divergence: rehearsal of R29 (compensating migration for the `migration_reproducibility_deep` divergence)

Clone: `$S/rehearsals/E-divergence`, branch `r29-rehearsal`, base `31142552` (its DB blob is `d874ba9e`'s, git blob `2d37c876`). Nothing in `/home/user/guidebook` was written; its `git status` shows only the harness's own appends (`commands.jsonl`, `transcripts/`).

## Verdict

**EXECUTABLE WITH CHANGES.** The divergence clears with no invented data: every restored value is read from a `--rebuild` (the migration chain), and the deep check goes from FAIL to PASS. Three things in R29 and the plan do not hold as worded:

1. **R29's OVERTURN condition is met.** It reads "a divergent value shown to be payload-backed and not reproducible by any verb". All 27 divergent `evidence_sources` values, and the one ORCID the bot added, match CrossRef payloads that research sessions persisted before the bot ran. No verb can write any of the seven columns. The revert still stands on other grounds: nothing that reaches the book reads these columns, and two of them hold the wrong kind of value. The overturn clause needs rewording (see the last section).
2. **The re-entry branch is empty, because it cannot be executed.** `--verify-authors` only verifies and writes nothing. `amend-source` refuses all seven columns. `correct-source` writes only `retrieval_log.PAYLOAD_FIELDS`, which contains none of them. Re-entering any value needs a tooling PR first (rule 10).
3. **The sanctioned capture path alone gives a migration that breaks `--rebuild`.** `emit_batch_sql.py` captures a delta against the blob. A compensating migration also replays against the chain, which still holds the original author rows, so the replay fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: evidence_source_authors.id`. The fix is 24 hand-added keyed `DELETE`s, marked in the file.

There is also an ordering constraint the plan does not state. The migration must land **after** step 1.5's deletion of `resolve-dois.yml` has merged. An offline replay of `resolve_dois.enrich_from_crossref`, using the persisted payloads, recreates the same divergence on the next scheduled run: 4 rows, 27 values and 24 author rows.

## (1) The divergence, reproduced

E-divergence (R29): **can be executed, but not as worded.** The deep reproducibility check goes from FAIL to PASS, and no data is invented: every restored value is read from a `--rebuild` of the migration chain. Everything ran in the clone `$S/rehearsals/E-divergence` (branch `r29-rehearsal`, three commits on top of `31142552`). The real repo shows only the harness's own transcript and command-log appends.

**What the divergence is.** Three bot commits wrote straight into the DB:
- `c4c84634` (2026-09-21): REF-01006
- `842bb74d` (2026-09-28): REF-01007
- `1876a7f8` (2026-10-05): REF-01009 and REF-01011
- `d874ba9e` (2026-10-12) wrote only a `pipeline_runs` row. Its "p4=1" re-queried REF-01011 and changed nothing; that counter counts CrossRef answers, not writes, so it repeats every week.

In total that is 4 `evidence_sources` rows and 27 values in 7 columns (`author_count_is_complete`, `journal_abbrev`, `issn`, `pub_month`, `language`, `subtype`, `citation_count`). The bot also deleted and re-inserted 24 author rows (same names, new ids and stamps, one ORCID added); the exemption hid those from the check. `pipeline_runs` now has 6 rows, not the 5 R2 states. Two runs (2026-08-24, 2026-09-07) predate the shallow history and can't be attributed.

**Are the values backed by saved payloads?** Yes, every one: all 27 values and the ORCID match CrossRef payloads that research sessions saved under `retrieval-log/` before the bot ran. But no verb can write any of the 7 columns: `correct-source` and `amend-source` refused all 14 probes. And nothing that reaches the book reads them.

**Verdict per part:**
- **Re-entry: cannot be done as written.** `--verify-authors` only checks; it writes nothing. A wanted value needs a tooling PR first, adding the column to `retrieval_log.PAYLOAD_FIELDS`.
- **Revert: done, with changes.** The capture through `emit_batch_sql` breaks `--rebuild` (`UNIQUE constraint failed: evidence_source_authors.id`), because it captures a delta against the DB while a migration also replays on the chain. Adding 24 keyed DELETEs by hand makes it converge. Counts: 27 values reverted (plus 8 timestamp/session stamps), 24 author rows restored (which drops the one ORCID), 0 re-entered, 0 undecided.
- **R29's overturn condition is met as worded** ("payload-backed and not reproducible by any verb"). The revert still stands because nothing in the book reads these columns, `journal_abbrev` is just a copy of `journal_name`, and `subtype` holds CrossRef's `type`. The clause needs to add "read by something that reaches the book".
- **Exemption narrowing: done, but it must ship as a separate tooling PR.** With `EXEMPT_TABLES = ("pipeline_runs",)` both reproducibility gates pass, and the deep check now compares the author table. The edits to the `reproducibility-invariant` criterion and the CLAUDE.md rule-3 sentence are owner merges. In one combined PR with the data migration, `research_tooling_separation` (rule 10) goes red; each half passes on its own.
- **Order neither the plan nor R29 states:** 1.5 merges, then the data PR, then the exemption PR, then OD-9. If the migration lands while `resolve-dois.yml` is still live, the next Monday run recreates the same divergence; an offline replay with the saved payloads confirmed this. The data PR also needs `regenerate_derived.sh`, or two blocking freshness gates go red (seen).
- **After 1.5 the divergence stops growing.** The only writers to the DB outside migrations are `resolve_dois.py` and `verify_urls.py`, both run only by the two workflows. `verify_urls.py` is dormant: it has no candidates today, but runs again 2026-10-15. `db.py` refuses the committed DB, and no hooks write it.

**Gates:**
- Baseline: 67 green, 7 examined nothing, 11 advisory red.
- After all three commits: 68 green, 7 examined nothing, 10 advisory red. Deep and `schema_walkability_fresh` went from red to green; `research_tooling_separation` turned red only because both PRs sit in one combined diff (each passes alone).
- `--selftest`, `schema_reference_audit` and `build_graph --check` are unchanged.
- `--rebuild`: same tables, views, triggers and indexes, and the same row counts except `pipeline_runs` (exempt).
- Size: +168 / −39 lines over 13 files, almost all the 128-line migration. The step adds more lines than it removes.

**Other defects found:**
- `correct-source --field authors` rewrites author rows even when nothing changed, drops ORCID, and reports `[]`.
- `correct-source --help` lists 7 fields where the code allows 9.
- `emit_data_migration`'s risky-pattern warnings don't fire on quoted identifiers, which is the form `emit_batch_sql` emits.
- `migration_reproducibility.py --selftest` already fails on base, and nothing runs it.
- The registry note's "six tables" is stale.

**Not verified:** the commits behind the two oldest `pipeline_runs` rows (shallow clone); whether any admission without a verification status lands before 2026-10-15. OD-9 itself was not executed; its callers are listed in the report.

Files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/db856d85-2082-5d35-9529-aa996506261b/scratchpad/rehearsals/`:
- E-divergence-report.md
- E-divergence.patch (10 MB, mostly regenerated one-line HTML)
- E-divergence.handmade.patch (the hand-made changes only)
- E-divergence_compensating_migration.sql
- E-divergence_divergence.tsv (the full difference, attributed to commits and payloads)
